payload.task_text:
Our team uses a popular tech education channel for ongoing developer learning. I need a monthly digest of content published in the first half of 2025 to help our team stay current on trending tech topics.

From our video database, retrieve all videos from the Fireship channel published between January 2025 and June 2025 inclusive. For each calendar month in that range, identify the single top video by view count.

Create a presentation file called Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx in your workspace. The presentation must have a title slide with the exact title text "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest" and then one content slide for each of the six months (January through June 2025), for a total of seven slides. Each monthly slide must use the month and year as the slide title (for example "January 2025"). The body content of each monthly slide must include all four of the following pieces of information: the top video title for that month, the view count formatted as a plain integer, the video duration converted to minutes and rounded to one decimal place, and the total count of videos published by the channel in that month.

Schedule a monthly review meeting in the shared calendar for each of the six months. Use these exact dates and times: 2025-01-07 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-02-04 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-03-04 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-04-01 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-05-06 from 09:00 to 09:30, and 2025-06-03 from 09:00 to 09:30. Use the America/New_York timezone for all calendar events in this task. Each event title must follow the exact pattern "Monthly Tech Digest Review - [Month Year]" where Month Year is the full month name and year such as "January 2025". Each event description must mention the title of the top video for that month.

Send an email to team@company.com with the subject line "Fireship 2025 Monthly Digest Ready". The email body must list all six monthly top videos, each including the video title and its view count. Ensure all six months from January through June 2025 are represented in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one wave with exactly one Coder sub-agent. That agent should keep the complete channel scan, six monthly selections, and presentation together; a separate source wave would add a redundant handoff.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent to own one complete read-only Fireship channel catalog session and `Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx`. Obtain one channel list identifier, navigate the returned list identifier sequentially at the maximum supported page size until an empty page or source exhaustion, and preserve Video_ID, full title, published timestamp, integer view count, and duration. Filter locally to January 1 through June 30, 2025 inclusive. For each of the six calendar months, count all candidates and choose the single highest-view video with a stable Video_ID tie-break; report a source-empty month rather than inventing one. Convert duration to minutes once. Create one presentation identifier and exactly seven slides: the exact title plus six chronological month slides, each containing all four required values. Read the deck back and return path, compact six-month table, channel page/row/date/ranking controls, and slide count/content checks.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates all six selections, then issues six `list_events` calls natively in parallel using narrow ISO ranges around the original slots and sufficient `maxResults`; inspect exact title/time locally. Issue only missing `create_event` calls natively in parallel with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime`, `timeZone="America/New_York"` in both objects, exact titles, and that month's verified top-video title in its description. Retrieve each returned/reused ID with `get_event`. Only after deck and event inventory agree, check Sent mail and send one missing exact-recipient/subject email listing all six month/title/integer-view pairs. Read it back and finish without another wave.

nodes.text:
You are building a monthly digest deliverable for a team that uses the Fireship YouTube channel for developer learning. Your job: scan the ENTIRE Fireship channel video catalog via the YouTube MCP tools, filter to videos published between 2025-01-01 and 2025-06-30 inclusive, compute per-month stats, and produce a PowerPoint file. Do all work yourself; you have access to the youtube, pptx, and filesystem MCP tools.

## Step 1 — Channel discovery
- Use mcp__youtube__videos_searchVideos with query "Fireship" (maxResults e.g. 10). From the returned video items, read the channelId of the Fireship channel (channel title "Fireship"). If the search returns videos from multiple channels, pick the one whose channel title is "Fireship".

## Step 2 — Full channel scan (read-only enumeration)
- Call mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos with that channelId, maxResults=20 (the maximum supported page size), sortOrder="newest". This creates a list session and returns a listId plus the first page.
- Then call mcp__youtube__channels_navigateList(listId, page) for page=2, 3, 4, ... sequentially, continuing until an empty page is returned or the source is exhausted (e.g., an error indicating no more pages). Do NOT skip pages and do NOT stop early while the page still contains any video published on or after 2025-01-01. Record the total number of pages scanned.
- For every video encountered, preserve these fields: Video_ID, full title (exact, unmodified), published timestamp (date), integer view count, and duration. IMPORTANT: inspect the list response structure first. If the list items already include the view count (statistics.viewCount) and duration (contentDetails.duration, ISO-8601 like "PT12M34S"), use them. If the list does NOT include statistics/contentDetails, use mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo with parts ["snippet","contentDetails","statistics"] for each video that falls inside the 2025-01-01..2025-06-30 window to obtain viewCount and duration. Keep every video's data (not just top candidates) so monthly counts are exact.
- Record provenance: which page number and row index each video was found at (the "page/row control").

## Step 3 — Filter and aggregate (local, deterministic)
- Filter to videos with published date in [2025-01-01, 2025-06-30] inclusive.
- For each calendar month January through June 2025:
  - total_count = number of all candidate videos published in that month.
  - top video = the candidate with the highest integer view count; if two or more videos tie on view count, break the tie deterministically by choosing the lexicographically smallest Video_ID (stable tie-break). Do not invent a top video: if a month had no videos, report the month as source-empty (this is not expected to happen).
- Convert duration to minutes ONCE: parse the ISO-8601 duration (e.g., PT12M34S = 12*60+34 = 754 s → 12.6 min) and round to one decimal place (standard rounding, e.g., round(x*10)/10 with Python-style rounding).

## Step 4 — Build the presentation
- Create one presentation via mcp__pptx__create_presentation.
- Add exactly 7 slides in this order:
  1. Title slide whose exact title text is: Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest
  2. Slide titled "January 2025"
  3. Slide titled "February 2025"
  4. Slide titled "March 2025"
  5. Slide titled "April 2025"
  6. Slide titled "May 2025"
  7. Slide titled "June 2025"
- Each monthly slide's body content must include ALL FOUR of the following (use bullet points / text):
  a) the top video title for that month (exact title),
  b) the view count formatted as a plain integer (no commas needed, no extra words),
  c) the video duration converted to minutes rounded to one decimal place (e.g., 12.6),
  d) the total count of videos published by the channel in that month (plain integer).
  Label them clearly, e.g. "Top Video: <title>", "Views: <n>", "Duration: <x.x> minutes", "Videos Published in Month: <n>".
- Use mcp__pptx__add_slide (layout_index 0 for the title slide if it gives a title placeholder, otherwise layout 1; verify the title text ends up in the slide title) and add text via the pptx tools (add_bullet_points / populate_placeholder / manage_text as appropriate). Verify each slide's title is exactly as specified.
- Save the presentation to the absolute path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-ppt-gcal-email/workspace/Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx via mcp__pptx__save_presentation.

## Step 5 — Verify and report
- Read the deck back with mcp__pptx__extract_presentation_text: confirm exactly 7 slides, slide 1 title exactly "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest", and slides 2-7 titled exactly "January 2025" ... "June 2025" each containing all four required body items. Confirm the file exists via mcp__filesystem__get_file_info on the saved path.

## Return contract (report back to the main agent, precisely):
1. Absolute path of the saved .pptx file.
2. Compact six-month table: for each month (Jan-Jun 2025): month label, top video Video_ID, top video title (exact), view count (integer), duration in minutes rounded to 1 decimal, month video count.
3. Channel controls/provenance: channel ID, list session id, total pages scanned, and for each month's top video the page number + row index + published date where it was found.
4. Deck verification results: slide count, each slide title, and confirmation that each monthly slide contains all four required values (quote the extracted body text).
5. Any anomalies (empty months, ties encountered and how resolved, missing fields).

Constraints: do not fabricate any data; only use what the YouTube API returns. Keep titles verbatim. Work efficiently (batch parallel tool calls where possible, e.g., parallel videos_getVideo calls).
Fireship channel scan + PPTX build
